correctness.rationale: Tree path resistances add; all-pairs maximum equals max_{i<j}(1/w_i+1/w_j), never the edge-only maximum. Let D this maximum and u_i=(1/w_i)/D. Then u_i>0, pair constraints u_i+u_j≤1, and D=sum c_i/u_i. Conversely F(u) with pair constraints gives a feasible allocation; a strict-inequality point can be scaled and improved. If all u_i≤1/2, F≥2C sharply only at u_i=1/2. Otherwise one unique u_j=t>1/2 forces other u_i≤1−t, yielding sharp strictly convex envelope c_j/t+(C−c_j)/(1−t). Its unique interior minimum exists exactly at 2c_j>C, gives t=sqrt(c_j)/(sqrt(c_j)+sqrt(C−c_j)), and all other u_i=1−t. For no-majority all t>1/2 produce >2C. These strict equality conditions establish global uniqueness including m=2/boundary. Independently generated 1,000 positive integer price vectors with 10,000 other normalized resistance samples verified bounds and exact budget/diameter; full-domain proof analytic.

value.rationale: Worst-case all-vertex-pair effective resistance is an independently motivated network-design objective. This complete pricing sensitivity classification resolves arbitrary star size and arbitrary positive prices; it reveals uniform unique optimum even under heterogeneous costs until a sharp majority-price bifurcation. The exact allocation formulas and threshold can guide star network budgets, not extrapolated to general graphs.

final_claim: On every star with m≥2 edges, positive edge prices c_i and conductance budget sum c_i w_i=1, unique resistance-diameter minimizer is uniform w_i=1/C with value 2C iff no c_i>C/2. Otherwise, for unique majority price c_j, optimal two-level conductances and diameter are explicit square-root formulas with strict improvement (sqrt(c_j)−sqrt(C−c_j))².
limitations: No claim about maximal resistance over edges alone or Kirchhoff index.
Finite sample is not an infinite optimality proof; strict convexity and pair inequalities provide it.
